trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight AC lands at 13:00, so morning is travel time. No activities scheduled before arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: After checking in at your Old Montreal accommodation, explore the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal on foot. Stop at historic bistros and cafés to taste local specialties like tourtière, poutine, and Quebec-style pastries. The tour is walkable directly from your hotel, making it perfect for your first afternoon. Take time to admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior and the Old Port waterfront at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the Old Port (Vieux-Port) waterfront along the St. Lawrence River. Enjoy the warm summer evening atmosphere, street performers, and free public spaces. Browse the night market vendors near the Clock Tower Pier for affordable local snacks and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Eaten before or during travel — grab a snack at the airport on arrival.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour tastings (~$15–25 CAD for self-guided snacking at market stalls and bakeries like Olive & Gourmando or a boulangerie on Rue Saint-Paul).
meals.dinner: La Banquise (open 24/7, ~$15–20 CAD) — a Montreal institution famous for affordable, generous poutine with dozens of topping variations. Located nearby and easy to reach by Metro or a short ride.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after the 13:00 arrival. Old Montreal is walkable from your hotel, minimizing transport costs. Keep luggage light for the afternoon walk. Weather should be warm (~25°C), so wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets. Pick up a OPUS transit card at the airport Metro station for ~$6 CAD to save on bus/Metro fares throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the Metro (Orange Line) to Jean-Talon station (~20 min, ~$3.75 CAD). Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruits, artisan breads, and local charcuterie from vendors. Arrive early (9:00–9:30 AM) for the freshest produce and a lively atmosphere. Budget $15–20 CAD for tastings and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Walk: After the market, walk or take the bus to the vibrant Plateau neighbourhood. Explore Rue Saint-Denis and Avenue du Mont-Royal for colourful murals, independent boutiques, and a quintessentially Montréalais atmosphere. Visit Parc La Fontaine (free entry) to relax by the lake and watch locals enjoy the summer sun.
day_by_day.evening: Schwartz's Deli and The Main Smoked Meat Experience: Head to the legendary Schwartz's Hebrew Delicatessen on Boulevard Saint-Laurent (open since 1928). Join the iconic queue — part of the authentic experience — and order a classic smoked meat sandwich on rye with a pickle and cherry Coke (~$15–18 CAD). Afterwards, walk along 'The Main' (Saint-Laurent Blvd) to enjoy the nightlife buzz without spending extra.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh bagel from St-Viateur Bagel (near Jean-Talon area) or from a market vendor at Jean-Talon — Montreal bagels are a must (~$2–4 CAD).
meals.lunch: Snack-style lunch from Jean-Talon Market stalls: a crepe, local cheese, fresh fruit, and maple taffy (~$12–18 CAD total). Eat al fresco in the market courtyard.
meals.dinner: Schwartz's Deli smoked meat sandwich combo (~$15–18 CAD). Arrive before 6 PM to beat the longest queues. Budget-friendly and iconic.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is open daily but is busiest and most vibrant on weekday mornings. Bring cash as some vendors prefer it. The Metro OPUS card from Day 1 covers all transit today. Parc La Fontaine is a great free afternoon option — bring a book or a picnic item from the market. Schwartz's is cash-preferred; there is an ATM nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park (Parc du Mont-Royal): Take the bus or walk up to Montreal's iconic green space designed by Frederick Law Olmsted (free entry). Hike or walk the trails to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic city views. Enjoy the fresh morning air and spot locals doing tai chi and jogging. This is a beloved free Montreal experience and a great way to start the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal en Lumière or Just for Laughs Festival Experience: July is peak festival season in Montreal. The Just for Laughs (Just pour rire) Festival runs in mid-July and features FREE outdoor performances, street food vendors, and live comedy acts on outdoor stages in the Quartier des Spectacles (Place des Arts area). Spend the afternoon enjoying free shows, browsing festival food stalls, and soaking up the incredible atmosphere. Check the festival schedule in advance at hahaha.com for free outdoor programming.
day_by_day.evening: Continue at the Just for Laughs Festival: The outdoor evening shows are the highlight — free street performances, impromptu comedy acts, and a buzzing crowd. Grab affordable festival street food for dinner (tacos, poutine, grilled corn, crêpes available from vendors at ~$8–15 CAD per item). Stay as late as you like; the festival atmosphere peaks after 7 PM.

meals.breakfast: Café Névé or any local dépanneur (corner store) near your hotel for a coffee and croissant (~$5–7 CAD). Alternatively, pick up supplies from a nearby IGA or Metro grocery store for a very budget-friendly breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mount Royal: Pack snacks from a dépanneur or bakery before heading up — sandwiches, fruit, and water (~$8–12 CAD). Eat at the lookout or on the grass near Lac des Castors.
meals.dinner: Just for Laughs Festival street food vendors in the Quartier des Spectacles (~$10–15 CAD). Look for Québécois comfort food like poutine, smoked sausage, or a Montreal-style hot dog (steamé).

day_by_day.notes: Check the Just for Laughs Festival website or app before the trip to confirm the 2027 free outdoor programming schedule — outdoor shows are always free. The Quartier des Spectacles is accessible by Metro (Place-des-Arts station, Green Line, ~$3.75 CAD). Mount Royal is best in the morning before the heat peaks. Wear sunscreen and bring a reusable water bottle — there are water fountains in the park.

day_by_day.morning: Mile End Neighbourhood & St-Viateur Bagel: Start your final morning in the beloved Mile End neighbourhood. Visit the original St-Viateur Bagel shop (open 24/7) and watch bakers hand-roll and wood-fire bagels in real time — buy a fresh sesame or poppy seed bagel for ~$1.50 CAD each. Walk along Rue Bernard and Avenue Laurier to browse independent bookshops, vintage stores, and street art murals that define this artsy, multicultural district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Marché Atwater (Atwater Market): Take the Metro (Green Line) to Lionel-Groulx station and visit Atwater Market, Montreal's other beloved public market. Browse local vendors selling Québécois produce, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and prepared foods. Walk along the Lachine Canal bike path (free) for beautiful views and a relaxed final afternoon. Rent a BIXI bike (~$3.50 CAD for a single 45-min ride) to cycle the canal path like a local.
day_by_day.evening: Final Evening in Old Montreal: Return to your home base in Old Montreal for a farewell stroll. Walk along Rue Saint-Paul, the oldest commercial street in Canada, as the golden hour light hits the stone buildings. Sit at a terrasse (patio) for a final drink or dessert. Watch street performers near Place Jacques-Cartier as a perfect, free send-off to Montreal.

meals.breakfast: Fresh St-Viateur bagels with cream cheese purchased from the shop (~$4–6 CAD for two bagels with schmear). Eat while walking through Mile End.
meals.lunch: Atwater Market lunch: Assemble a picnic from market vendors — a wedge of local cheese, cured meats, a baguette, and seasonal fruit (~$12–16 CAD). Enjoy it along the Lachine Canal.
meals.dinner: Le Passé Composé or a comparable affordable bistro on Rue Saint-Paul in Old Montreal — look for a table d'hôte (prix-fixe) dinner deal (~$20–28 CAD for 2–3 courses). Alternatively, grab a final crêpe or gyro from a street vendor near Place Jacques-Cartier (~$10–12 CAD) to keep costs minimal.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday mornings are the best time to visit Atwater Market — it's lively and fully stocked. BIXI bike-share stations are located throughout the city; download the BIXI app to locate docks. If departing on a late flight or the next day, store luggage at your hotel or at Gare Centrale (luggage lockers available). Budget summary for the trip: accommodation aside, aim for $40–60 CAD per day on food and $10–15 CAD on transit, keeping the total trip spend very manageable.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight AC arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Old Montreal hotel, check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: After settling in, step right out of the hotel and join a guided culinary walking tour through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Stop at historic bistros, artisan bakeries, and cozy cafés to taste local specialties like tourtière, poutine, and Quebec artisan cheeses. Perfect introduction to the city's food culture without traveling far from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Old Port waterfront as the sun sets over the St. Lawrence River. Explore Place Jacques-Cartier, a lively public square filled with street performers and local vendors. Enjoy the warm summer evening atmosphere before heading to dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or on arrival — no breakfast scheduled given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Snack on tastings included during the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour (Quebec cheeses, charcuterie, baked goods) — a light and authentic mid-afternoon introduction to local flavors.
meals.dinner: Chez Boulay – Comptoir Boréal (Old Montreal area): A mid-range bistro celebrating Nordic-Quebec cuisine with dishes like wild mushroom risotto and Arctic char. Expect $30–50 CAD per person. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage light for the walking tour — the hotel is within easy walking distance of all evening spots. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro from Old Montreal to the Jean-Talon Market in Little Italy — one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. Join a guided food tour sampling fresh Quebec cheeses, maple syrups, heirloom vegetables, local charcuterie, and seasonal summer fruits. Engage with passionate local vendors and learn about Quebec's agricultural heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighborhood Festival Stroll: Head to the vibrant Plateau-Mont-Royal neighborhood, known for its colorful staircases, independent boutiques, and thriving arts scene. Explore any ongoing street festivals or art events happening in mid-July (Montreal's festival season is in full swing). Browse local artisan stalls, catch live music, and soak up the distinctly Montréalais street culture.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière or Just for Laughs Festival Experience: July is peak festival season in Montreal. Attend Just for Laughs (Juste pour rire), one of the world's largest comedy festivals, which runs throughout July. Enjoy free outdoor performances, street food vendors, and live entertainment in the Quartier des Spectacles. A quintessential Montreal summer evening.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico (Mile End / Plateau area, en route to Jean-Talon): A legendary Montreal café beloved for its espresso and simple pastries. Budget-friendly at under $10 CAD.
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh baguette, local charcuterie, Quebec cheese, and seasonal fruit from market stalls. A delicious, affordable, and authentic picnic-style lunch for around $15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Au Pied de Cochon (Plateau-Mont-Royal): An iconic Quebec institution known for indulgent dishes like duck in a can and foie gras poutine. Mid-range splurge at $40–60 CAD per person — worth every cent for the experience. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most vibrant on weekday mornings — arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM for the best experience. Check the Just for Laughs festival schedule at hahaha.com for specific free outdoor show times. Metro Line 5 (blue) connects Jean-Talon to the Plateau efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Schwartz's Deli and The Main Smoked Meat Experience: Make the pilgrimage to Schwartz's Hebrew Delicatessen on Boulevard Saint-Laurent — a Montreal institution since 1928. Join the iconic queue (arrive early to beat the lunch rush) and savor a legendary smoked meat sandwich with a side of coleslaw and a pickle. This is a bucket-list Montreal food experience. Afterward, explore the lively Saint-Laurent Boulevard (The Main) corridor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mount Royal Park Exploration: Take a leisurely hike or walk up Mount Royal, the city's beloved green lung designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Enjoy panoramic views of Montreal's skyline from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. In July, the park often hosts Tam-Tams, an informal Sunday drum circle and gathering (check if any mid-week events are scheduled). Rent a paddleboat at Beaver Lake for a relaxing afternoon on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for another evening of Just for Laughs festival programming or explore the Latin Quarter (Quartier Latin) for live music at local bars and terrasses. Montreal's terrasse culture is at its peak in July — enjoy drinks and light bites outdoors under the warm summer sky.

meals.breakfast: Fairmount Bagel (Mile End): One of Montreal's two legendary bagel bakeries, open 24/7. Grab freshly baked sesame or poppy seed bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon for a true Montreal morning ritual. Under $10 CAD.
meals.lunch: Schwartz's Deli: The smoked meat sandwich with sides IS lunch. Budget $20–25 CAD including a drink. Simple, historic, and unforgettable.
meals.dinner: Terrasse on Rue Saint-Denis (Quartier Latin): Choose from several mid-range bistros with outdoor terrasse seating. Try L'Express — a classic French-Quebec brasserie with steak frites, onion soup, and excellent house wine. Around $35–50 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Schwartz's opens at 8:00 AM on weekdays — arriving by 8:30 AM avoids the worst queues. The smoked meat is slow-cured for 10 days and is best ordered 'medium' fat. Mount Royal is a 20-minute walk from the Plateau or a short bus ride. Bring water and sunscreen for the park — expect 25°C and sunny skies.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal Morning Exploration: On your final morning, revisit Old Montreal at a leisurely pace without a tour agenda. Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica (book AURA light show or a morning visit, $15 CAD entry), explore the Pointe-à-Callière Museum of Archaeology if interested, or simply wander the quieter morning streets before the tourist crowds arrive. Browse the weekend artisan market at Place du Marché Bonsecours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mile End Final Wander: Spend the afternoon doing a relaxed final loop through the Plateau and Mile End neighborhoods. Pick up local souvenirs — Quebec maple products, local hot sauces, artisan goods — from independent shops on Avenue Laurier or Rue Bernard. Visit a local fromagerie for Quebec cheese to bring home. This is a low-key, enjoyable way to spend a final afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: End the trip with a memorable dinner back in the Old Montreal neighborhood, close to the hotel. Celebrate the trip with a proper sit-down meal featuring Quebec's best seasonal produce.

meals.breakfast: Olive + Gourmando (Old Montreal): A beloved local café and bakery known for exceptional breakfast sandwiches, granola bowls, and freshly baked pastries. A perfect Old Montreal morning spot. Budget $15–20 CAD. Arrive early as queues form quickly on weekends.
meals.lunch: Marché des Saveurs du Québec (Jean-Talon area or Old Port): A specialty shop and café showcasing exclusively Quebec-made products. Grab a light lunch of local ciders, cheeses, and charcuterie boards for $20–30 CAD — a great final taste of the province.
meals.dinner: Toqué! (Old Montreal): Montreal's most celebrated farm-to-table restaurant, helmed by legendary chef Normand Laprise. A fitting farewell dinner showcasing the best of Quebec's seasonal ingredients. Tasting menu available; expect $80–120 CAD per person. Reserve well in advance. Alternatively, for a more casual farewell, try Garde Manger (Old Montreal) at $50–70 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Notre-Dame Basilica is a short walk from the hotel — buy tickets online to avoid queues. If departing early the next day, pack bags the night before and confirm checkout time with the hotel. The Old Port area is particularly lively on Saturday evenings in summer — consider a final evening stroll along the waterfront after dinner to close out the trip on a high note.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Montreal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh produce, and local charcuterie. Chat with vendors and discover the heart of Montreal's culinary scene.

experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Plateau neighborhood during one of its many street festivals or art events, browsing local boutiques, murals, and terrasse cafés. Sample bagels from the famous St-Viateur Bagel shop and soak in the bohemian local culture.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer by private luxury car service to your Old Montreal hotel. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: Begin your Montreal experience with a guided culinary walk through the historic cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Stop at intimate historic bistros and artisan cafés to taste signature Québécois dishes — think tourtière bites, local charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and house-made pâtisseries. The tour weaves through Place Jacques-Cartier and along the waterfront, giving you a rich sense of the city's French heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a landmark Old Montreal fine-dining restaurant. Head to Toqué! or Maison Boulud for a world-class tasting menu showcasing the best of Québec's seasonal produce, foraged ingredients, and premium seafood — perfectly paired with a curated wine selection from an award-winning cellar.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack at the hotel or a quick stop at a charming Old Montreal café such as Olive + Gourmando for a pressed sandwich and locally roasted coffee.
meals.dinner: Toqué! (447 Place Jean-Paul-Riopelle) — Québec's most celebrated fine-dining institution. Opt for the grand tasting menu with wine pairings for a true luxury introduction to the city's culinary scene.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless arrival. Ask the hotel concierge to confirm the culinary walking tour booking and reserve dinner at Toqué! well in advance — tables are highly sought after. Pack light layers for the evening as Old Montreal's waterfront can have a gentle breeze even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to one of North America's greatest open-air markets in the Little Italy neighborhood. A knowledgeable guide leads you through the vibrant stalls sampling raw-milk Québec cheeses, artisan maple syrups and taffy, heirloom tomatoes, freshly baked baguettes, smoked meats, and seasonal fruit. Meet the passionate local producers who supply Montreal's top restaurants and pick up gourmet provisions to enjoy later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighborhood Festival Stroll: Make your way to the iconic Plateau neighborhood, which in mid-July is alive with street festivals, outdoor art installations, and live music. Browse the eclectic boutiques along avenue Mont-Royal, discover local street art in the laneways, and soak up the effortlessly cool, creative atmosphere that defines this beloved quarter. If a specific street festival is running, enjoy free outdoor performances and artisan food vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Just for Laughs Festival Experience: Montreal's legendary Just for Laughs (Juste pour rire) festival runs throughout July, filling the Quartier des spectacles with free outdoor performances, comedy galas, street entertainers, and food village vendors. Catch a headline outdoor show or splurge on premium gala tickets for a world-class comedy performance at one of the indoor venues.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium café stop near Jean-Talon Market — try Café Olimpico on St-Viateur for an authentic espresso and fresh pastry in true Montréal Italian-neighbourhood style.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a curated picnic assembled from Jean-Talon Market's finest offerings — artisan cheese, charcuterie, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit — savoured in Parc Laurier in the Plateau.
meals.dinner: Le Filet (219 Avenue Mont-Royal Ouest) — a refined, intimate restaurant in the Plateau celebrated for its creative small plates, impeccable seafood, and natural wine list. Perfect for a leisurely pre-festival dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best experienced early — aim to arrive by 9:00 AM for the freshest selection and fewest crowds. Check the Just for Laughs festival schedule in advance at hahaha.com and book any premium gala tickets ahead of time. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the full day of exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Schwartz's Deli and The Main Smoked Meat Experience: Make the pilgrimage to Schwartz's Hebrew Delicatessen (est. 1928) on boulevard Saint-Laurent — a true Montreal institution. Arrive early to beat the queue (or use a concierge-arranged skip-the-line option) and indulge in the city's most legendary smoked meat sandwich: hand-sliced, perfectly fatty, and served on rye with yellow mustard and a dill pickle. This is a bucket-list Montreal moment. Afterward, explore the surrounding Mile End neighbourhood, stopping at the iconic St-Viateur Bagel shop to see hand-rolled, wood-fired bagels being made.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure and luxury at your hotel or a curated cultural experience: Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Archaeology Museum in Old Montreal for a fascinating journey beneath the city's streets to discover its Indigenous and colonial foundations. Alternatively, book a private rooftop pool session or spa treatment at your hotel to recharge before the evening festivities.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière or Just for Laughs Festival Evening: Return to the Quartier des spectacles for another immersive festival evening. If Montreal en Lumière programming overlaps, enjoy illuminated art installations and gourmet food village tastings. Otherwise, cap the night at a Just for Laughs outdoor gala or a late-night comedy club set in the festival village, followed by a nightcap at one of Old Montreal's rooftop bars.

meals.breakfast: In-room hotel breakfast or room service — indulge in a full Québec-style spread with local maple syrup, fresh fruit, and Viennoiserie delivered to your room.
meals.lunch: Smoked meat experience at Schwartz's Deli (3895 Boulevard Saint-Laurent) — the iconic medium-fat smoked meat sandwich is the only order you need. Follow with a fresh sesame bagel from St-Viateur Bagel.
meals.dinner: Monarque (406 Rue Saint-Jacques) — a stunning brasserie in Old Montreal housed in a grand heritage building, serving elevated French-Québécois cuisine with an exceptional raw bar and one of the city's finest cocktail programs.

day_by_day.notes: Schwartz's does not take reservations — arrive by 10:30 AM on a weekday to minimize wait time, or ask your hotel concierge about VIP arrangements. St-Viateur Bagel (263 Rue Saint-Viateur Ouest) is open 24 hours — a warm, fresh bagel straight from the oven is unmissable. Book dinner at Monarque in advance for a Friday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Old Montreal: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Afterward, take a private guided walking tour of Old Montreal's hidden gems — secret courtyards, the magnificent Notre-Dame Basilica interior (book a premium visit for the AURA light show if available in the morning), and the scenic Vieux-Port waterfront. Browse the artisan galleries and boutiques along rue Saint-Paul for unique Québécois souvenirs and local art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mile End Final Exploration: Return to the Plateau for a final leisurely afternoon. Visit the vibrant Marché des Saveurs du Québec at Jean-Talon for last-minute gourmet gifts — fine maple products, ice ciders, and artisan preserves. Stroll through Parc du Mont-Royal via the scenic Olmsted trail for panoramic city views, then wind down with a cocktail on a sunny terrasse on avenue Laurier.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Luxury Dinner: End your Montreal journey with an unforgettable dinner at one of the city's most prestigious addresses. Reserve a table at Maison Boulud (in the Ritz-Carlton Montreal) for a refined French-inspired tasting menu in one of the most elegant dining rooms in Canada, complete with sommelier-guided wine pairings and impeccable service — the perfect send-off for a premium Montreal experience.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast — request a champagne breakfast or room service spread as a final morning treat.
meals.lunch: Terrasse William Gray (421 Rue Saint-Amable) — a stunning rooftop restaurant in the heart of Old Montreal with sweeping views over the historic district. Enjoy a refined weekend brunch with Québec-sourced dishes and a classic Bloody Caesar cocktail.
meals.dinner: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton (1228 Rue Sherbrooke Ouest) — Daniel Boulud's Montreal flagship offering an exquisite tasting menu with French technique and Québec terroir. Reserve the chef's table or garden terrace for a truly memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange a late checkout if your departure flight allows. Book the Notre-Dame Basilica AURA experience (basiliquenddm.ca) in advance as it sells out quickly on weekends. Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton requires advance reservations — contact them at least one week ahead and mention any special occasion for a personalized experience. Arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure.
